steps.title: Establish the common experiential operating model and protect early international and global opportunity capability
steps.summary: Undertake the institutional review already planned for 2.2.2 and use it to establish the common operating model for experiential opportunity. In parallel, protect international employer-engagement activity that is already live but unsupported by dedicated resource: appoint one G6 Employer Relations & Insights Manager (International) from October 2026, add one G5 Employer Relations & Insights Adviser focused on East Asia from January 2027 for the second half of the academic year, and provide £15,000 of international employer-facing and in-country activity funding in 2026/27. Also bring the G6 Global Mobility Opportunity Development Manager forward to January 2027 so that purposeful outward-mobility opportunity development begins during the first investment year. Map how King’s currently creates, holds, manages and activates external relationships across faculties, Careers & Employability, SASD, IES, Advancement and Alumni and other relevant areas. Define the shared process through which experiential opportunities are sourced, designed, approved, promoted, delivered, supported and evaluated, with common templates, agreements and standards where these reduce duplication. Delivery remains distributed; the operating model should make local activity easier, safer and more consistent rather than centralising it.

outputs.summary: A G6 Global Mobility Opportunity Development Manager is in place from January 2027 to begin building, brokering and translating a broader mix of purposeful outward-mobility opportunities before the second Global Mobility post joins in 2027/28.

steps.title: Mobilise UK experiential infrastructure and complete the Global Mobility opportunity-development team
steps.summary: Use 2027/28 to establish the four-post UK Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development team and add the G5 Global Mobility Opportunity Development Officer from September 2027, completing the two-post Global Mobility opportunity-development capability begun with the G6 in January 2027. Retain the G6 International Manager, East Asia G5 and Global Mobility G6 for the full year and move the international activity envelope to £50,000. The UK team comprises one G6 Experiential Partnerships & Opportunity Development Manager, two G5 Experiential Opportunity Development Advisers and one G5 Experiential Partnerships Operations & Intelligence Adviser. With the UK team and Global Mobility G5 September starts modelled at ten months and the already established roles budgeted for the full year, the 2027/28 direct in-year budget is £438,932; the annualised exit run-rate at the end of the year is £483,319.

steps.title: Mature, evaluate and settle the business-as-usual model
steps.summary: Operate and evaluate the infrastructure throughout the investment window rather than waiting for the full team to be in place. Track UK experiential opportunity throughput, partner experience, international employer relationships and activity, Global Mobility opportunity growth, Graduate Transitions reach and progression once live, financial-access demand and wider recruitment and reputation benefits. Use evidence to refine the faculty or sector portfolios of the two UK opportunity-development advisers, international regional priorities, common processes and the longer-term recurrent operating model. By June 2029, confirm the enduring workforce and operating model so that activity from July 2029 onward is clearly treated as business as usual, benefits realisation and ongoing service improvement rather than a further mobilisation year.

outputs.title: Evidence-led recurrent operating model agreed by June 2029
outputs.summary: King’s confirms the enduring workforce and service model, including what transfers into business as usual, what can be repurposed and whether the staged staffing model remains proportionate to demonstrated demand and benefit.
